maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection tweak merged to canary we saw host CPU and parse latency jump ~2.2x on streaming small-chunk workloads. Repro and initial flame pasted below. This looks like tokenization + parse + kv cache churn stack.

maria: Repro steps (local canary):
```
# run the streaming harness (10k small requests)
./harness --mode=stream --seq-len=64 --chunk=64 --concurrency=40 --target=canary-host:8080
```
Logs: host parse time p50 -> 6.4ms from 2.8ms, CPU % per pod +70%.

maria: Relevant pprof (sampled, 10s):
- 34% host::parse::tokenize
- 22% host::stream::frame_parse
- 18% kvcache::evict
- 9% grpc::writev
- 7% net::write

pprof: https://perf.internal/pprofiles/1809998881 (private)

ryan: :eyes: any recent change in how we format cache keys or the kernel-selection path? that kv evict spike looks suspicious.

ash: Putting a note: kernel-selector now sets "mini_batch_hint" lower on canary for throughput reasons. smaller mini-batches + more writev flushes could increase parse overhead per token.

kai: I pulled a trace — miss rate jumped: canary ~43% vs prod ~12% on same workload. keys look identical length but I see different header ordering (we switched to canonicalized header order in proto->json). Possibly key normalization regression.

lee: If key bytes differ by ordering we'll end up with cold kvcache inserts for every request -> churn. That matches evict numbers. Maria can you paste a raw key example?

maria: example kv key (hex, shortened):
```
old: 0a2f6b6579..len:72..hash:ab12
new: 0a2f6b6579..len:74..hash:ff3c  (note: extra 2 bytes for header order)
```

maria: Also noticed grpc write pattern changed: more frequent 512B frames (instead of coalesced 4k). Could be from mini-batch change or proto framing tweak.

ash: quick hypothesis: kernel-selection lowered batch size -> fewer tokens per batch -> more frequent prefix parse -> kvcache keys include transient ordering field -> high miss rate -> evictions -> CPU spike.

ryan: Can we validate by forcing previous kernel selector behavior locally? Toggle env KERNEL_HINT=legacy to reproduce.

maria: did that — with KERNEL_HINT=legacy: p50 parse down to 2.9ms and miss rate back to ~14%. So it's strongly correlated.

kai: OK, root cause likely twofold: (1) kernel hint change reducing batching and affecting writev/flush patterns, (2) a subtle key normalization change in the proto->key path that added nondeterministic ordering. Both together amplify.

lee: Quick fixes candidates: revert canonical header reorder in key pipeline OR add a stable key serializer for kvcache (cheap). Also consider forcing a min batch size in kernel selector until we fix.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) patch kernel selector to respect min_mini_batch=8, 2) patch kvcache key serializer to sort header fields deterministically. I can open PRs.

perf-bot: perf alert created: ID perf-1809998881. Baseline p50 parse 2.8ms -> canary 6.4ms. Alert routed to #eng-runtime oncall.

ryan: Sounds good. Maria if you open PRs drop the before/after pprof links and I'll help validate on canary.

maria: Will do. PRs:
- kernel: https://git.redwood/infer/commit/ab12/ (draft)
- kvcache key: https://git.redwood/infer/commit/cd34/ (draft)

ash: Also add a microbenchmark for small-chunk streaming (sequence len 64) to CI so we catch regressions.

kai: I can add telemetry check to watch kvcache miss % post-deploy (flagged anomaly if >20% over 5m).

lee: :thumbsup: prioritize kvcache key serializer first (lower blast radius).

maria: Will queue both PRs and run the microbench locally. Thanks all.

maria: follow-up: I'll post updated pprof + canary numbers here when PRs land.
